searchText: Tricky bit we ran into though, we allowed miners to include any message they wanted to, regardless of the base fee, but the miner has to pay the difference if that messages fee cap is below the base fee, capped at the block reward. Since its a testnet, and miners wanted to maximize the throughput, they just packed their blocks entirely full, spiking up the base fee astronomically I could potentially see miners doing this in Eth if beetcoin farming becomes more profitable to miners than foregoing block rewards and tx fees Though that would definitely be a weird edgecase <@!91365817869946880> You mean the miners were paying for transaction gas themselves? As in, miners were paying for *other people's* transactions? I think someone given the proof that miners still paying for transaction gas themselves. > I could potentially see miners doing this in Eth if beetcoin farming becomes more profitable to miners than foregoing block rewards and tx fees This doesn't have to be miners. *Anyone* could spam the network with transactions to raise the base fee, and it would cost them exponentially more the longer the kept it up. I'm not worried about such a vector personally. 👍 💯 Rumours #1559 cancelled ? Instead of EIP1559 EIP2929 deployed.? you mean these rumours? https://twitter.com/sassal0x/status/1304306341759000577 It was meant to be a joke 🙂 <@456226577798135808> I also asked > As in, miners were paying for *other people's* transactions? <@!301186049323958275> Yep, because the incentives of the network made that make sense to them I support 1559

> I could potentially see miners doing this in Eth if beetcoin farming becomes more profitable to miners than foregoing block rewards and tx fees
This doesn't have to be miners.  *Anyone* could spam the network with transactions to raise the base fee, and it would cost them exponentially more the longer the kept it up.  I'm not worried about such a vector personally.
